audit_items.proof_trace: `util_rate = debt / (debt + cash - cash_reserve)` exceeds 1.0 whenever `cash_reserve > cash`, a condition reachable because `accrue_interest` (L125-149) increases `cash_reserve` by `reserve_factor * interest` without adjusting `cash` or re-asserting the invariant; the only guard (`cash >= cash_reserve.ceil()`) lives solely in `withdraw_underlying`. In a near-fully-utilized pool (e.g. `cash=1`, `debt=10000`), even a modest reserve_factor and elapsed time causes `cash_reserve > cash`, yielding `util_rate > 1.0` and causing `calc_interest` to return a borrow rate that linearly exceeds `max_borrow_rate`.
audit_items.attack_scenario: A pool at ~99.99% utilization (cash=1, debt=10000, cash_reserve=0) accrues interest over time; once `reserve_factor * accumulated_interest > cash - cash_reserve` (e.g., `reserve_factor=0.1`, `interest=20` → `cash_reserve=2 > cash=1`), every subsequent `accrue_interest` call uses a borrow rate above `max_borrow_rate`, compounding debt faster than the governance model allows and risking depositor withdrawal denial because `withdraw_underlying` asserts `cash >= cash_reserve.ceil()`.
